chunks: And they did not estimate Allah with true estimation when they said, 'Allah did not reveal to any man a thing.' Say, 'Who then revealed the Book that Moses brought, a guidance and light for the people? You make it into separate sheets, displaying some and concealing much. And you were taught what neither you nor your fathers knew.' Say, 'Allah.' Then leave them in their vain discourse to play.

key_terms.الْكِتَابَ: The Book (specifically the Torah in this context)
key_terms.حَقَّ قَدْرِهِ: True estimation of God's power and status
key_terms.قَرَاطِيسَ: Separate sheets or pieces of paper

ai.seo_question: What is the evidence against those who claim God did not reveal anything to a human?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often linked to the claim of the Ahl al-Kitaab that revelation ceased with the Torah, thereby denying the prophethood of Muhammad (PBUH) and the finality of the Quran. It underscores the continuity of divine guidance through human messengers, affirming that the same God who revealed the Torah to Moses is the source of the Quran. The critique of partial disclosure and concealment reflects the scholarly view that previous scriptures were altered or selectively interpreted by their custodians.
